title: The Regiment of the Cape Route
premise: In 1797 Cape Town, under the shifting flags of empire, apprentice clockmaker Oscar Thornbury is summoned to the observatory to repair its failing master clock, the instrument by which every ship on the Cape Route sets its longitude. Hidden inside the clock he finds coded naval orders, and at his door a child appears with a note: forget this face. As Oscar repairs the mechanism, he uncovers a conspiracy to falsify the observatory's time and wreck or spare convoys for profit, forcing him to choose between the quiet life of invisible hands and the dangerous truth. In the end, Oscar sends the true time signal, loses the workshop to fire, but gains a family: the child, whose face he refuses to forget, and Elise, the astronomer's daughter who taught him that some hours are worth dying for.
about_author: Lena Lockridge is a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing logbooks from Dutch and British colonial ports before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage on the Atlantic coast, where she restores antique clocks badly and plots novels well.

chapters.title: The Hour That Would Not Hold
chapters.summary: Oscar Thornbury, POV. Summoned at dawn to the observatory, Oscar inspects the master clock and finds its escapement deliberately damaged, not worn. His master warns him to fix it quietly and ask nothing. Emotional beat: unease beneath professional pride; Oscar senses the clock was silenced on purpose.

chapters.title: A Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A girl of seven appears at his lodging with a sealed note reading 'forget this face' and no name. He cannot turn her out. Meanwhile the observatory's astronomer, Van Reenen, watches him too closely. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness cracking Oscar's practiced invisibility.

chapters.title: Gears and Ghosts
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Working nights in the clock tower, Oscar discovers a hidden compartment containing coded tables of times and ship names. He copies nothing, tells no one, but sleeps badly. The child, whom he calls Sparrow, begins helping with small tasks. Emotional beat: curiosity warring with self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Astronomer's Daughter
chapters.summary: Elise Van Reenen's POV. Elise, who secretly does her father's calculations, notices the clock's errors don't match any mechanical fault. She suspects the new apprentice and tests him with a deliberately wrong figure. Emotional beat: wary mutual recognition between two people hiding their competence.

chapters.title: Time Sold by the Knot
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Deciphering fragments, Oscar realizes the clock's time has been skewed minutes at a stretch, enough to misplace entire convoys at sea. A broker named Corvijn visits the tower openly, as if he owns it. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Forget This Face
chapters.summary: Sparrow's POV (childlike voice). Sparrow reveals she was told to deliver herself and be forgotten; she remembers a woman's hands and a ship's bell. Oscar promises, against all sense, not to forget her. Emotional beat: the child's loneliness mirroring Oscar's own.

chapters.title: Longitude of Lies
chapters.summary: Elise's POV. Elise confronts Oscar in the tower; they compare evidence and realize her father is either complicit or coerced. Their alliance forms over star charts at midnight. Emotional beat: love kindling in the space where trust should be cautious but isn't.

chapters.title: The Broker's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Corvijn offers Oscar a fortune to finish the repair 'as instructed,' revealing he knows about Sparrow. Oscar refuses and immediately regrets the refusal's cost. That night the workshop's windows are smashed. Emotional beat: fear arriving as arithmetic—what safety costs.

chapters.title: What the Pendulum Remembers
chapters.summary: Elise's POV. Elise searches her father's papers and finds letters proving he falsified time under threat to his family, including an illegitimate daughter—Sparrow. Emotional beat: grief and fury braided together as loyalty to blood collides with truth.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Minutes Fast
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A convoy is due; the conspirators need the clock twenty-two minutes fast to lure it onto the Haakklip reef. Oscar must stall the repair without revealing his sabotage. Emotional beat: the terrible intimacy of holding lives in a hairspring.

chapters.title: The Face He Was Told to Forget
chapters.summary: Elise's POV. Elise meets Sparrow and recognizes her half-sister; she says nothing to her father yet. Oscar and Elise argue about whether truth or protection comes first. Emotional beat: first real fracture between them—love tested by competing duties.

chapters.title: Van Reenen's Confession
chapters.summary: Van Reenen's POV. Cornered by his daughter, the astronomer confesses: Corvijn holds his debts and his daughter's existence as leverage. He begs Elise to let one more convoy die. Emotional beat: a broken man's shame; pity curdling into contempt.

chapters.title: The Signal Station
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar travels to the coastal signal station and confirms the navy receives its time solely from the observatory clock—one corrupted source, total power. He drafts a plan to broadcast true time independently. Emotional beat: purpose replacing fear.

chapters.title: Sparrow Taken
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Returning, Oscar finds Sparrow gone; Corvijn's men left a note naming the price: the clock finished fast, the child returned unharmed. Emotional beat: rage and helplessness; invisibility finally impossible.

chapters.title: The Bargain
chapters.summary: Elise's POV. Elise offers herself to Corvijn as collateral in Sparrow's place, buying three days while pretending to cooperate. She passes the plan to Oscar through a hidden note in a watch casing. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered calmly, terror underneath.

chapters.title: Hairspring
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar builds a portable chronometer from workshop scraps—a second source of true time—and races to verify it against the stars with Elise's calculations smuggled from the house. Emotional beat: craftsmanship as resistance; hope measured in seconds.

chapters.title: The Night of the Convoy
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Storm night: the fleet approaches, the false clock runs fast, Corvijn waits at the tower, Elise stalls him, Oscar climbs to the signal lanterns. Emotional beat: breathless convergence; every thread pulled taut.

chapters.title: True Noon
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. At the critical minute Oscar signals the corrected time; the convoy alters course off the reef. Corvijn's men seize him, but sailors who owed their lives intervene. Emotional beat: triumph inseparable from peril; the strike of the true hour.

chapters.title: Fire in the Workshop
chapters.summary: Elise's POV. Retaliating, Corvijn burns Oscar's workshop; Oscar saves only his tools and Sparrow's delivered note. Van Reenen publicly testifies, breaking Corvijn's leverage at the cost of his name. Emotional beat: loss transfigured—the things burned were never the treasure.

chapters.title: Corvijn's Ledger
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Using the coded tables, Oscar and Elise expose Corvijn's wrecking ledger to the Admiralty; he flees the Cape rather than hang. Justice is partial, but real. Emotional beat: bitter satisfaction; some accounts balance late, not never.

chapters.title: The Clockmaker's Daughter
chapters.summary: Sparrow's POV. Sparrow, formally taken in by Oscar and Elise, asks if she may call the repaired clock hers. Van Reenen, disgraced but free, teaches her the stars. Emotional beat: chosen family assembled from the forgotten.

chapters.title: The Regiment of the Cape Route
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, years later. The rebuilt workshop keeps the true time for every ship rounding the Cape; Oscar, Elise, and Sparrow stand as the clock strikes. He finishes the repair, keeps the promise, and is remembered. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace—time, at last, on their side.
